subject: Re: Billing floor and compute-window alignment for interleaved prompts
body_preview: Question about whether minimum billing is applied per API call vs per aggregation window when using interleaved short prompts/streaming.
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightretail.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@brightretail.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing behavior for interleaved short prompts and streaming

Hi Tessa —

Quick question from our engineering and finance teams after reviewing May's bill (see attached invoice_snippet_May.pdf): when BrightRetail issues lots of short streaming requests that are interleaved (e.g., a 12-token prefix, then a 40-token continuation, then a new 8-token prefix), our invoice shows a surprisingly high floor charge compared to raw token counts. Can you confirm whether Redwood's minimum billing floor is applied per individual API request, or per some aggregation/compute window?

Example we pulled:
- 9:12:03 AM: request A — 12 tokens (stream on)
- 9:12:04 AM: request B — 41 tokens (continuation)
- 9:12:07 AM: request C — 8 tokens (new prompt)

On our side we expected token charges close to ~61 tokens total, but invoice shows rounding up to the equivalent of ~128 tokens for that burst. Is that expected? If so, can you share the exact rounding rules and if any credits apply for shared KV cache / prefix reuse?

We can hop on a quick 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks —
Samir
VP Product, BrightRetail

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Billing behavior for interleaved short prompts and streaming

Samir —

Thanks for the clear example and the invoice snippet. Short answer: Redwood meters in short aggregation windows to balance cost vs latency; minimums can look amplified for tightly interleaved short requests. I want to give you the exact formula that was used to generate the line-item you saw.

High level (non-sensitive summary):
- Metering uses a rolling aggregation window (30s by default for hosted customers) to group requests that hit the same serving pool.
- Within that window we compute effective billed tokens using per-request tokenization, then apply a per-call floor and finally a window-level rounding that snaps the summed total to the model's billing quantum.
- Prefix/KV reuse can reduce billed tokens, but only when requests are routed to the same hot shard and the KV cache hit is material (>5 tokens).

To make this concrete, can you share a 24-hour sample of the request timestamps and token counts (CSV is fine)? I asked Vanessa to prepare a worked example and a toy spreadsheet that walks through the arithmetic so you can validate the numbers yourself.

If helpful, we can also run a one-month pilot waiver (partial credit) for well-characterized bursts while you tune batching on your side. I'll leave the plan details to Vanessa.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 13:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing behavior for interleaved short prompts and streaming

Samir —

Attaching a worked example (billing_example_breakdown.xlsx) that mirrors your 3-request burst and expands to a few more cases to show edge behaviors. Summary of the example:

Case A (three tight requests, same shard):
- Raw tokens: 12 + 41 + 8 = 61 tokens
- Per-request floor: our platform enforces a 16-token floor per request if the request latency path is < 250ms and no batching occurred (so each small request counts for at least 16 tokens) => 16 + 41 + 16 = 73 tokens
- Window quantum rounding: after summing, we round to the model quantum (32-token quantum for this model) => next quantum boundary is 96 tokens billed
- Effective billed tokens: 96 (matches what you saw on the invoice line item)

Case B (same sequence but requests joined into a micro-batch or delayed by up to 40ms so they reach the same batch):
- Batching merges two small requests into a 28-token unit + 41 = 69 raw tokens
- Floors apply differently (only on batch-level synthetic request) => fewer floors triggered; post-quantum rounding yields 64 or 96 depending on exact grouping.

Cache/KV rules: if the 8-token prompt reuses the same prefix and the cache is warm, the billed token delta can be reduced by the cached KV tokens (we show an example where billed goes from 96 -> 64 on cache hit). Cache behavior is nondeterministic across shard failovers; we flag warm-cache sessions when the cache hit rate > 70% for the 1-minute window.

Pilot: we can apply a one-time credit that neutralizes the first month's quantum-rounding delta while you experiment with batching thresholds. That would be a manual credit against invoice BR-4521; I'll coordinate with Billing (Kim) for the authorization.

I'll keep the spreadsheet annotated with the formula cells.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
